## AMAZONE

**Where:** 4:00 & C · **From:** Porto Alegre · **Landmark:** green/yellow feathered headdress portal · **Year:** 2026

Draws its spirit from the Amazon - the largest river system on Earth and one of the most biodiverse places in existence. We are a Brazilian-rooted community that honors South American heritage while welcoming people from all over the world into our family. We believe in showing up fully: to work, to celebrate, to heal, and to connect. Our camp is built around that commitment, offering a rich mix of ceremonial and embodied experiences: Amazonian plant medicine, ice plunges, vibroacoustic therapy, ecstatic dance, cacao ceremonies, and the kind of music and food that makes strangers feel like family. Come for the pizza. Stay for the community. 2026 marks our 10th burn. We have every reason to celebrate and we intend to.

*More: http://www.brazilianburners.com*

## Art Support for Bass Snail

**Where:** G & 4:15 · **From:** Boise · **Landmark:** glowing snail and BASS SNAIL banner. · **Year:** 2026

Welcome to the high-desert hub for the Bass Snail Mutant Vehicle and the Idaho Conclave. Located at the intersection of heavy machinery and flow arts, our camp is a vibrant gateway for the Idaho creative community. When the Bass Snail is docked, visitors can explore the art car, meet the builders, and collect commemorative stickers and patches. Seeking a break from the dust? Relax under our 400 square feet of public shade, a welcoming street-side sanctuary where you can watch the Idaho Conclave during daily flow rehearsals and workshops. Whether you are here to talk shop with our mechanics, demystify fire safety with performers, or find a friendly place to park your bike, we invite you to experience the Gem State on playa. Look for the glowing snail and the flickering flames.

## Castra Ursi

**Where:** 4:00 & F · **From:** New York City · **Landmark:** Look for the field of solar panels and glowing art · **Year:** 2026

A fully solar-powered camp exploring what a fuel-free future on Playa can look like. This year we present The Last Ocean, an interactive installation built from reclaimed ocean and ocean-bound plastic. Step onto the platforms and walk, run, and dance across a solar-powered sea of light as the surface responds to movement with shifting waves of color. The entire artwork and camp operate 100% on solar energy with no fuel or petrol used in any capacity. Solar panels are integrated directly into the space, making the renewable energy system that powers the experience visible to everyone who visits. Castra Ursi also shares open diagrams and build information showing how our solar and battery systems work, helping other camps explore how to build their own fuel-free infrastructure.

*More: https://www.jenlewinstudio.com/portfolio/the-last-ocean/*
